messages:
Maria P.: Heads-up — seeing a ~8-12% p95 latency regression after we flipped kernel-selector v3 last night. Root looks like prefill-heavy requests. @Chen W. can you confirm staging traces?

Chen W.: Yep, confirmed on staging. Prefill batches are growing (avg tokens/batch up ~30%) and KV cache warmups spike, which pushes decode into queue starvation. quick paste from perf_top: `prefill_queue_wait 43%`, `kv_warmup 21%`, `decode_gpu_util 12%`.

Sarah L.: Interesting. So kernel-selector is picking the more aggressive fused-kernel for prefill which is great for throughput, but combined with batch formation heuristics it creates long prefill windows. Decode flaps.

Maria P.: Exactly. Two levers here: (1) batching policy (how we form prefill vs decode batches, token budgets) (2) kernel affinity/selection rules for phase. I want to try a small runtime heuristic: a "drift controller" that nudges prefill token_budget_target down when recent decode latency cross a threshold, with hysteresis to avoid thrash.

Chen W.: Sketch: maintain moving_avg_decode_latency (window 60s) and moving_avg_prefill_tokens. If decode_p95 > SLA * 1.1 then reduce prefill_target = max(min_prefill, prefill_target * (1 - alpha)) where alpha = clamp((decode_p95/SLA - 1), 0, 0.25). Add hysteresis: only apply if condition holds for 3 consecutive windows.

Sarah L.: Also add a kernel_affinity score to avoid always picking fused kernels for prefill when seq_len variance high. Simple rule: if seq_len_stddev > X then prefer stable fp16 kernel for prefill to shorten warmup tails.

Maria P.: Agree. Proposed config snippet for the canary run:

```
batching: {
  prefill_target_tokens: 120,
  decode_target_tokens: 32,
  prefill_min_tokens: 48,
  prefill_max_tokens: 240,
  drift_controller: {
    window_s: 60,
    hysteresis_windows: 3,
    min_alpha: 0.05,
    max_alpha: 0.25,
    sla_multiplier: 1.1
  }
}
kernel_selection: {
  phase_affinity: {
    prefill: ["fp16_stable", "fused_fast"],
    decode: ["fused_fast", "fp16_stable"]
  },
  seq_len_stddev_threshold: 64
}
```

Chen W.: I can wire the controller into the metrics stream and expose a debug endpoint `/debug/prefill-drift` that outputs decisions + recent windows. I'll also dump flamegraphs: `flame_prefill_2175.svg` and `flame_decode_2175.svg`.

Sarah L.: For canary: route 1% of traffic on dedicated hosts with the new runtime flag `enable_prefill_drift_controller=true`, collect p50/p95/p99 for both prefill and decode, kv-hit latency, and kernel switch counts.

infra-bot: deploy-bot started canary: roll 1% -> hosts r-42..r-46. (automated note)

Maria P.: Good. Chen, can you add a small synthetic workload that produces interleaved long prefill + short decode sequences so we stress the queue separation? Also log per-request `phase_kernel` chosen.

Chen W.: On it. I'll push the experiment branch and a small benchmark harness by EOD. Putting the dashboard panels: `decode_latency_by_phase`, `prefill_tokens_by_batch`, `kv_warmup_rate`.

Sarah L.: If this reduces decode p95 by >10% with <=1% throughput loss, we keep. If not, rollback and iterate.

Maria P.: Sounds good. Followups: @Chen W. create PR with the controller + debug endpoint; @Sarah L. create canary dashboard and define success criteria. I'll watch the canary results and coordinate rollback. :thumbsup:

Chen W.: PR drafted: `runtime/prefill_drift_controller` -> will link when ready.

Sarah L.: Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123/prefill-drift-canary (private).

Maria P.: Thanks — keeping this short. We'll reconvene after first 30m of canary.

(quick notes: avoid changing packing kernel heuristics in the same window as this canary; separate change would confound results)
